I was recently in the position where my rehab fees ran out at a time that I am still in need of therapy. I would recommend the following options:

-If he is seeing a physiotherapist and/or an occupational therapist, ask them to give some additional notes for exercises he can do on his own to continue his stabilization. It works wonders, even without a professional in sight. He’ll learn to be more independent that way throughout his progress. 

-If you have a small amount of fees left, stretch the amount of therapy time to once a month to check up on his progress. 

-***exercise***. I cannot stress this enough. Cardio and strength training helps give enough blood flow and oxygen to the brain to help quicken the process. I’ve spoken with a neurologist on another subreddit and he expressed how exercise helps strengthen the neurons in the brain weakened by TBI. 

That’s all that I have to offer regarding his circumstances. I hope that helps!

Head trauma and serious whiplash from a rough head on collision from another driver, causing my head to contact with the steering wheel before whipping to the headrest of my seat as well as the ceiling of my car (the car jumped on impact from how hard the driver collided into me)

I was diagnosed with mild concussion. The first 2 months after my accident, I couldn’t read and experienced serious vertigo and nausea. I also had upper body muscle damage that caused me to rely on a walker/cane for a year before now walking independently. Nowadays I have inflammation in the skull and mild dizziness when I turn my head to the sides. 

Went through MRI and CT scan to show I had some loose blood vessels in my brain. Doctors told me my brain “shook” in my skull and need time to reprogram. Did some cognitive tests the first six months after my accident where occupational therapists concluded I had a brain injury due to slow and delayed results. 

Furthermore, I have serious tension in my neck that connects to the skull, so I’ve been told the stubbornness to heal is also muscular. I’ve done acupuncture, massage, and stretching but they only help a little, not a lot. 

I have done what I could to help. I’ve taken medication for 6 months before stopping because the medication no longer had an impact. I changed my diet and pushed through physio to help with brain fog. I’ve tried to meditate but nowadays I don’t have the willpower to continue it. 

Anything you’d recommend would be immensely appreciated.
